verdict: U.S. Bancorp hit record revenue of $7.9B as fee income jumped 13% — helped by a first full quarter of BTIG in capital markets — and kept $2.2B as profit.

kpis.label: Capital markets revenue
kpis.note: +69% YoY — first full quarter with BTIG

segments.name: Net interest income
segments.note: Interest earned on loans and securities, minus the interest paid on deposits and borrowings — the bank's core engine. The net interest margin widened to 2.84%.

segments.name: Noninterest income
segments.note: Fee income: trust and investment management fees ($802M), capital markets ($640M), merchant processing ($461M), corporate payments ($457M) and card revenue ($440M), partly offset by $65M of securities losses.

opex.name: Compensation & benefits
opex.note: Pay and benefits for the bank's workforce — its biggest cost, up 7% YoY.

opex.name: Technology & communications
opex.note: Technology and telecoms — up 19% YoY on investment in the platform.

opex.name: Other intangibles
opex.note: Amortization of intangible assets from past acquisitions.

opex.name: Professional, marketing & other
opex.note: Professional services ($115M), marketing and business development ($199M) and other costs ($324M).

takeaways.title: Fees did the heavy lifting
takeaways.text: Noninterest income rose 13.1% to $3.5B, led by capital markets revenue up 69% to $640M in the first full quarter including BTIG. Net interest income added a steadier 5.8% growth to $4.5B.

takeaways.title: Costs stayed on a leash
takeaways.text: The efficiency ratio — costs per dollar of revenue — improved to 55.9% from 57.2% a year ago, and return on tangible common equity was 18.5%.

takeaways.title: Credit losses are contained
takeaways.text: The bank set aside $654M for credit losses while actual net charge-offs ran at 0.51% of loans, improved from 0.56% a year ago.

footerNote: U.S. Bancorp headlines taxable-equivalent net interest income of $4,490M (total revenue $7,970M); this page uses GAAP net interest income of $4,468M (total revenue $7,948M), which does not change net income. For a bank, the provision for credit losses plays the role of cost of revenue. Net income attributable to U.S. Bancorp was $2,202M.
